## Recommended learning resources

- [R for Data Science, 2nd edition](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) by Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Garrett Grolemund. A more comprehensive R text that inspired the *teaching format* of this independent resource.
- [Hands-On Programming with R: Getting Started](https://rstudio-education.github.io/hopr/starting.html). An accessible installation and introductory guide.
- [R project and language](https://www.r-project.org/) and [CRAN packages](https://cran.r-project.org/).
- [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
- [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/), including [Quarto books](https://quarto.org/docs/books/) and [GitHub Pages publishing](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html).
- [`refugees` R package website](https://populationstatistics.github.io/refugees/) and [population dictionary](https://populationstatistics.github.io/refugees/reference/population.html), [applications dictionary](https://populationstatistics.github.io/refugees/reference/asylum_applications.html), [decisions dictionary](https://populationstatistics.github.io/refugees/reference/asylum_decisions.html).
- [UNHCR Refugee Data Finder](https://www.unhcr.org/refugee-statistics/).
- [UNHCR data visualization guidance](https://dataviz.unhcr.org/).

## Attribution and data notes

The fixed ten-origin example is transcribed from numerical results in the `refugees` package documentation for 2022 (sum of reported `refugees` and `oip` by origin). The **five fictional asylum decision countries** are entirely invented for teaching percentages and are never evidence about any real asylum system. Other code chunks use the `refugees` package directly when rendered, so their results depend on the package version installed at render time.

This book is original instructional material. It is inspired by the step-by-step pedagogy of *R for Data Science*, but it is not a reproduction of the text, code or illustrations from that book.

## A simple reproducibility record

When completing an exercise or reproducing a figure, save the R commands **and** include the output of:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
packageVersion("refugees")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] '2025.12.2'
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
R.version.string
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "R version 4.5.2 (2025-10-31 ucrt)"
```


:::
:::


`sessionInfo()` provides a more complete record of your computing environment. You may record the date you retrieved or rendered the data, plus any filtering choices and definitions.
